name: EBNER RES (SUSAN)
address: 2348 NW TOWER ROCK RD, BEND, OR 97703

fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly, as it is the only access point for emergency vehicles.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs overhanging the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Designate and keep clear a flat area on the open lawn for emergency vehicle turnaround, since no dedicated turnaround space is visible.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence to reduce the risk of fire spreading directly to the structure.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the detached structure for the same reason.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear so responders can move between the two structures on foot without obstruction.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so it can be used as a staging area during an emergency response.
• Thin the dense vegetation bordering the property to allow responders to approach or reposition around the structures if the access drive is blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees on all sides of the structure to create more open space between the tree canopy and the building.
• Remove shrubs and grass growing directly against the exterior walls of the structure.
• Trim lower branches on trees near the structure so branches do not extend close to the roofline or walls.
• Thin the dense tree clusters around the structure to reduce the amount of connected vegetation leading toward the building.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow in groups near the structure so fire cannot travel easily between them.
• Mow or cut grass around the structure, particularly during dry periods when grass is most likely to carry fire.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead material from within shrub groupings near the structure.
• Thin scattered trees between the tree clusters and the structure to break up the continuous path of vegetation toward the building.
• Clear grass and low shrubs along the edges of the driveway to maintain a clear travel path for vehicles.
• Move any stored materials, woodpiles, or debris away from the structure and into more open areas away from surrounding vegetation.
